items.title: Pathwalker
items.summary:
A file reader allowing users to load pages from the file system. Can you escape the intended directory and uncover hidden server secrets?
TL;DR Pathwalker is an introductory web challenge illustrating a Path Traversal (Directory Traversal) vulnerability. The application passes an unsanitized page parameter to file_get_contents() . By supplying dot-dot-slash ( ../ ) directory traversal sequences, an attacker can traverse up out of the restricted ./page/ directory and read arbitrary files across the server, including flag.php . Source Code Analysis The target application features simple dynamic content retrieval:

items.title: Hide and Seek
items.summary:
Can you see me? I’m so close to you, but you can’t see me.
TL;DR Hide and Seek is an introductory web challenge testing fundamental source code review. The flag is embedded directly within the homepage HTML source code, hidden from the graphical viewport using styling or whitespace comments. Viewing the raw DOM source exposes the secret. items.title: Scoreboard
items.summary:
Check out the scoreboard! DO NOT ATTACK or scan the scoreboard; you don’t need to do that.
TL;DR Scoreboard is a web reconnaissance challenge emphasizing the importance of examining raw HTTP response headers. The challenge instructions strictly prohibit aggressive fuzzing or vulnerability scanning. Requesting the server headers via curl -I reveals a custom HTTP header (x-flag) exposing the flag directly.
